title: Ursa Minor
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45f6824d00778c707bcbc2d79290e87d384f85f3.png) Pixel Art: Ambition, Sulfox, and Charles

Sulfox the fennec fox celebrated his 20th birthday with great joy as he received a special gift — a pixel game named World Rebuilder. In this game, he plays the role of an interstellar explorer who journeys toward Polaris, the brightest star in the constellation Ursa Minor, and terraforms planets along the way.

A game level can be determined by a target sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ and a tool sequence $b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_m$. At the beginning of this level, there are $n$ (the length of the target sequence) continents with initial altitudes of $0$, arranged circularly around the equator of the planet where Sulfox landed.

The "Batch Edit" tool allows Sulfox to modify the altitudes of the continents simultaneously. Whenever he uses it, he should firstly select a number $k$ from the tool sequence and choose an arbitrary **real number** $x$. Then, he can select exactly $k$ **consecutive** continents and add $x$ to each of their altitudes. The level is cleared when the altitudes of the $n$ continents, starting from some continent in some direction, are $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ in order.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf9a3f1c4c6ac02b7686cf1b7693d6ff8e28e365.png) Figure: How to adjust the altitudes with the "Batch Edit" tool (The selected continents are highlighted)

In fact, the level designer for this game is quite a lazy guy, for he generated each level by selecting a contiguous subsequence from a global target sequence $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_N$ and a global tool sequence $B_1,B_2,\ldots,B_M$ respectively. What's worse, he didn't even bother to check whether each level is possible to clear, leaving Sulfox stuck at some levels marked as "easy"!

Luckily, as a video game, it certainly has multiple version updates to fix bugs (or maybe introduce new bugs, who knows?). Now given the global target sequence $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_N$ and the global tool sequence $B_1,B_2,\ldots,B_M$ in the initial version, you need to handle $Q$ events of two kinds:

- Game Update: Change the value of $A_p$ to $v$ in a new version.
- Level Query: Query if Sulfox can clear the level determined by target sequence $A_l,A_{l+1},\ldots,A_r$ and tool sequence $B_s,B_{s+1},\ldots,B_t$ in the latest version if he can use the tool any number of times.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $N$, $M$, and $Q$ ($1 \le N, M, Q \le 2 \times 10^5$), denoting the length of the global target sequence, the length of the global tool sequence, and the number of events, respectively.

The second line contains $N$ integers $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N$ ($0 \le A_i \le 10^9$), denoting the global target sequence in the initial version.

The third line contains $M$ integers $B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_M$ ($1 \le B_i \le N$), denoting the global tool sequence.

Then, each of the next $Q$ lines contains an event in one of the following two formats:

- `U p v` ($1 \le p \le N$, $0 \le v \le 10^9$), denoting an update that changes the value of $A_p$ to $v$ in a new version.
- `Q l r s t` ($1 \le l \le r \le N$, $1 \le s \le t \le M$), denoting a query of if Sulfox can clear the level determined by target sequence $A_l, A_{l+1},\ldots, A_r$ and tool sequence $B_s, B_{s+1},\ldots, B_t$ in the latest version. It is guaranteed that each value of $B_s, B_{s+1}, \ldots, B_{t}$ does not exceed $r - l + 1$.

## Output

For each query, output "`Yes`" in one line if Sulfox can clear the level determined by the given target sequence and the given tool sequence in the latest version, or otherwise, output "`No`" in one line.
statementZhMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45f6824d00778c707bcbc2d79290e87d384f85f3.png) 像素画：Ambition、Sulfox 和 Charles

耳廓狐 Sulfox 开心地度过了自己的 20 岁生日，因为他收到了一份特别的礼物——一款名为 World Rebuilder 的像素游戏。在这款游戏中，他扮演一名星际探险家，朝着小熊座中最亮的恒星北极星前进，并沿途改造行星。

游戏中的一个关卡由目标序列 $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ 和工具序列 $b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_m$ 确定。关卡开始时，Sulfox 所降落的行星上有 $n$（即目标序列的长度）块大陆，它们沿着赤道环形排列，初始海拔均为 $0$。

“批量编辑”工具可以让 Sulfox 同时修改多块大陆的海拔。每次使用时，他需要先从工具序列中选择一个数 $k$，并选择任意一个**实数** $x$。然后，他可以选择恰好 $k$ 块**连续的**大陆，将它们的海拔都加上 $x$。当从某块大陆开始，沿某个方向依次读出的 $n$ 块大陆的海拔为 $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ 时，即可通关。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf9a3f1c4c6ac02b7686cf1b7693d6ff8e28e365.png) 图示：如何使用“批量编辑”工具调整海拔（选中的大陆已高亮显示）

事实上，这款游戏的关卡设计师相当懒惰，他只是分别从全局目标序列 $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_N$ 和全局工具序列 $B_1,B_2,\ldots,B_M$ 中各选取一个连续子序列，就生成了一个关卡。更糟糕的是，他甚至懒得检查每个关卡是否能够通关，导致 Sulfox 卡在了一些标为“简单”的关卡上！

幸运的是，作为一款电子游戏，它当然会通过多次版本更新来修复漏洞（也可能引入新的漏洞，谁知道呢？）。现在给定初始版本中的全局目标序列 $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_N$ 和全局工具序列 $B_1,B_2,\ldots,B_M$，你需要处理 $Q$ 个事件，事件分为以下两类：

- 游戏更新：在新版本中，将 $A_p$ 的值改为 $v$。
- 关卡询问：询问在最新版本中，若 Sulfox 可以使用任意多次工具，他能否通过由目标序列 $A_l,A_{l+1},\ldots,A_r$ 和工具序列 $B_s,B_{s+1},\ldots,B_t$ 确定的关卡。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $N$、$M$ 和 $Q$（$1 \le N, M, Q \le 2 \times 10^5$），分别表示全局目标序列的长度、全局工具序列的长度以及事件的数量。

第二行包含 $N$ 个整数 $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N$（$0 \le A_i \le 10^9$），表示初始版本中的全局目标序列。

第三行包含 $M$ 个整数 $B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_M$（$1 \le B_i \le N$），表示全局工具序列。

接下来 $Q$ 行，每行包含一个事件，格式为以下两种之一：

- `U p v`（$1 \le p \le N$，$0 \le v \le 10^9$），表示一次更新，在新版本中将 $A_p$ 的值改为 $v$。
- `Q l r s t`（$1 \le l \le r \le N$，$1 \le s \le t \le M$），表示一次询问：在最新版本中，Sulfox 能否通过由目标序列 $A_l, A_{l+1},\ldots, A_r$ 和工具序列 $B_s, B_{s+1},\ldots, B_t$ 确定的关卡。保证 $B_s, B_{s+1}, \ldots, B_{t}$ 中的每个值都不超过 $r - l + 1$。

## 输出格式

对于每次询问，如果在最新版本中，Sulfox 能够通过由给定目标序列和工具序列确定的关卡，则单独一行输出“`Yes`”；否则，单独一行输出“`No`”。
